newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks flat, hamstrung by low selling.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks flat, hamstrung by low selling.

text.p: Sri Lanka closed barely moved in low turnover due to a lack of sellers, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.81 points up at 641.88. Ceylon Brewery rose three rupees to 46, National Development Bank 25 cents to 198.50.
Turnover was 9.3 million rupees on 444,987 shares.
"There is a lot of local institutional buying interest among low valued shares. But the problem is that there are no sellers," said Dihan Dedigama, a trader at brokerage John Keells.
Foreign buyers were out of the market due to a lack of blue chips that they favour, brokers said.
Foreign buying was worth 961,367 rupees while selling amounted to 238,000 rupees.
Sellers were on the sidelines waiting for first quarter 1997 corporate results, which are expected to be good, brokers said.
